conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I understand you came in with chest pressure. Can you tell me more about what happened?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’ve had this off and on for two days. Yesterday it was really bad—right in the center, lasted over an hour. I felt nauseous and was sweating a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And today you felt weak and dizzy, is that right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. My mouth was dry, and I just felt awful. My PCP told me to come in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good call. We’ve checked your heart enzymes and EKG. The good news is no sign of a heart attack. But your kidney function was a bit off—creatinine was up to 1.5, which is higher than your baseline.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh. I’ve had that before when I’m dehydrated. I’ve been skipping my IV fluids because of the leg biopsies coming up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. Your mitochondrial disease makes you more sensitive to dehydration, and that can trigger chest pain. We’re giving you 2 liters of IV fluids now to help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not my heart this time?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We can’t rule it out completely, but your EKG showed only minor changes, and your enzymes stayed negative. Your cardiologist wants you to do a stress echo tomorrow to be sure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You did the stress test this morning. I have the results—your heart function is normal, no signs of blockages or ischemia.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. So what caused the pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Most likely, it was due to dehydration, which we know can worsen angina in your case. Your creatinine is already back down to 1.2 after the fluids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my Plavix? I’ve been off it for five days for the biopsies.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve restarted it. You’re back on all your usual meds—Plavix, aspirin, metoprolol, the works. We switched your aspirin to chewable again, same as last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, good. I remember that helped last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning to discharge you today. You’re stable, pain-free, and labs look good.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. Should I restart my regular IV fluids at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, please. Staying hydrated is key, especially with your mitochondrial condition. Keep up with your appointments with your PCP and cardiologist.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. Thanks for explaining everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll have your discharge papers ready soon. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick check before you leave. Any chest pain since this morning?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: None at all. I feel much better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Excellent. Remember to take your meds as prescribed and follow up with your doctors.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your ride is here. You’re cleared to go home. Call if you have any chest pain, dizziness, or trouble breathing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ll stay on top of my fluids and meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor.
